answer: Coordination price via reflection budget.** Each agent identity gets a per-epoch quota of accepted coordination messages, throttled by a kernel that charges senders when their messages converge with many others in the same round. Distinct, independent agents rarely co-move, so honest senders pay little; a sybil cluster pushing one outcome pays steeply as its correlation score rises. This turns a fable of cheap many-voice influence into a real bill, and caps a sonnet-scale campaign the way a fixed budget caps any mass mailing.
